financials_interim.notes: Company (standalone, non-consolidated Asia Siyaka Commodities PLC) column of the same filing. operating_profit derived as Gross Profit 224,319,983 + Other Income 4,204,489 - S&D 10,336,050 - Admin 125,118,290 = 93,070,132, which ties to disclosed PBT after net finance cost (93,070,132 - 45,744,573 + 9,650,742 = 56,976,301). EPS 0.14 = 37,003,920/260,000,000 (company has no minority interest, it's the parent entity). short_term_borrowings excludes lease liabilities (current 11,718,267 + non-current 27,385,804) per the same convention as the GROUP row above.

Q1 is the first quarter of FYE 31 March, so Quarter figures = Cumulative figures (both columns identical in the filing). operating_profit taken from the Segmental note's Group 'Profit from operating activities' total (329,285,409), which is independently reproducible from the primary P&L (Gross Profit 619,479,934 + Other Income 3,946,676 - Selling&Distribution 22,947,242 - Admin 271,193,959 = 329,285,409) and ties exactly to PBT after deducting net finance cost (finance cost 82,421,434 - finance income 4,117,979 = 78,303,455; 329,285,409-78,303,455=250,981,954 = disclosed PBT). Balance sheet identity and EPS (=attributable profit/260,000,000 shares) both tie exactly, no column-swap ambiguity found. short_term_borrowings = 'Interest Bearing Borrowings on Client Financing' (3,239,014,987) + Bank Overdraft (54,326,622); IFRS16 lease liabilities (current 57,392,060 + non-current 221,656,375) are deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings fields (treated as lease obligations, not debt facilities) -- consistent with the same convention used for LOFC and LDEV entered in this same session. New segment: 'Manufacturing' (blended fertiliser, via subsidiary) is entirely new this year (Revenue Rs.382.5m vs Rs.0 in Q1 2025/26).

interim_updates.note_text: Asia Siyaka Commodities PLC (ASIY), the Colombo-listed tea/rubber/produce broker and agri-trading group, reported a very strong Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): Group revenue rose 51.0% YoY to Rs.1,497.3m from Rs.991.9m, gross profit nearly doubled (+87.4% to Rs.619.5m), and PAT more than quadrupled (+353% to Rs.170.7m from Rs.37.7m), driven by a turnaround across all three reporting segments. The Trading segment (agri-commodities and packing materials) swung from an operating LOSS of Rs.12.2m in Q1 FY2025/26 to a profit of Rs.138.8m this quarter on revenue of Rs.786.2m (+11.5%), the single largest driver of the group's profit growth. A brand-new Manufacturing segment (customised blended fertiliser) contributed Rs.382.5m of revenue and Rs.66.3m of operating profit that did not exist a year ago. The core Services segment (tea brokering, warehousing, logistics) grew revenue 14.7% to Rs.328.5m and profit 33.2% to Rs.124.2m. Finance costs rose 129.6% YoY to Rs.82.4m, reflecting a larger client-financing book (Interest Bearing Borrowings on Client Financing grew to Rs.3,239.0m from Rs.2,855.4m at 31 March 2026) used to fund tea-client advances -- the net income from this client-advancing operation (interest earned less interest paid on the funding) grew to Rs.64.0m from Rs.43.2m. Non-controlling interests (51% held via AgriOne Solutions) swung from an NCI LOSS of Rs.5.3m a year ago to an NCI profit of Rs.51.5m this quarter, consistent with AgriOne's ramp-up (it signed a new 5-year warehousing lease in June 2026). At the standalone Company level (the parent entity only, excluding subsidiaries), PAT actually fell 4.6% YoY to Rs.37.0m from Rs.38.8m, showing that essentially all of the group's profit growth this quarter came from the subsidiaries (Trading and the new Manufacturing segment), not the parent's own tea-brokering operations.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for ASIY -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY comparison uses only this filing's own 30 June 2025 comparative column (both P&L and Statement of Financial Position provide genuine YoY comparatives here, unlike LOFC's SOFP in this same batch).
interim_updates.takeaway: Headline Group PAT growth of +353% YoY is real but concentrated in two places outside the core brokering business: a Trading-segment turnaround (from a Rs.12.2m loss to a Rs.138.8m profit) and a brand-new Manufacturing segment with no prior-year comparative (Rs.66.3m profit) -- Company-level (parent-only, excluding subsidiaries) PAT was actually down 4.6% YoY, so investors should not extrapolate the consolidated growth rate to the group's traditional tea-brokering franchise.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +51.0% YoY to Rs.1,497.3m; PAT +353% YoY to Rs.170.7m (attributable to equity holders +177.2% to Rs.119.1m)
Trading segment swung from an operating loss of Rs.12.2m (Q1 FY25/26) to a profit of Rs.138.8m on revenue of Rs.786.2m (+11.5%)
New Manufacturing segment (blended fertiliser) contributed Rs.382.5m revenue and Rs.66.3m profit with no prior-year comparative
Finance costs +129.6% YoY to Rs.82.4m as client-financing borrowings grew to Rs.3,239.0m (from Rs.2,855.4m at 31 March 2026) to fund tea-client advances
Non-controlling interests (51%-held AgriOne Solutions) swung from an NCI loss of Rs.5.3m to an NCI profit of Rs.51.5m
Corporate guarantees issued by the Group to banks stood at Rs.3,200m (Asia Siyaka Warehousing, on behalf of parent) and Rs.1,500m (parent, on behalf of AgriOne Solutions) at quarter-end
key_drivers: Trading segment (agri-commodity/packing-material purchase and resale): operating result swung Rs.151.0m YoY, from a Rs.12.2m loss to a Rs.138.8m profit -- the single largest driver of consolidated profit growth
New Manufacturing segment (customised blended fertiliser, via subsidiary): Rs.66.3m of profit with zero prior-year base, adding a full new profit stream
Client-financing finance costs: +129.6% YoY (Rs.35.9m to Rs.82.4m) as the tea-client advance book grew, partly offset by growth in net client-financing income (Rs.43.2m to Rs.64.0m)
